transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm... I'm a barber. And I'm here because... well, it's gotten bad at work. I just... I'll do pretty much whatever it takes to get out of using the straight razor. Switch clients with someone else, tell them I can't find the blade, just hide it away. And if I absolutely have to use it... I just shake the whole time.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about using the straight razor even when you're not at work, like when you're at home or thinking about going into the shop?
I... I'm not really sure. I try not to think about work when I'm at home. So, I haven't really noticed. I just know it's bad when I'm actually there.
Outside of work, do you find yourself avoiding other situations where you might feel judged or embarrassed, like speaking in public or eating in front of others?
No, not really. I just... I don't like using the razor. That's all.
When you're not at work, do you ever feel anxious or avoid doing things because you're worried about something bad happening, even if it's not related to the razor?
No. I don't... I don't think so. I just go about my normal day, mostly. It's really just the razor.
When you have to use the straight razor, do you ever feel like your heart is racing, you're short of breath, or like something terrible is going to happen — like a panic attack?

Yeah. Um... the second someone asks for a razor shave, or... or if I just see the blade flipped open, it happens. My chest gets really tight. My hands start sweating a lot. It's... it's like my body just wants to back away before I even have time to think about it. It feels pretty bad.
Does your heart always race and do you always feel that way when you have to use the straight razor, or does it happen only sometimes?
Yeah... it's always. Like I just said, the second they ask for it, or if I even see the blade... it just happens. Every single time.
Is your anxiety specifically limited to the straight razor, or does it also happen with other tools or tasks at work that are less intense or common, like using clippers or scissors?

No, it's... it's just the razor. I can use clippers and scissors all day fine. I know it's just a tool I trained with, but... when that straight razor is sitting open at my station, it just feels like I'm about to hurt somebody, or... or cut myself badly. It's just that one thing.
